transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-21 11:00am PT / Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Torres (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (BrightLedger SRE), Alex Chen (BrightLedger Head of ML), Maria Lopez (BrightLedger CTO), Diego Ramos (BrightLedger Platform)

Summary: Quick retrospective on the pilot gate, review of initial benchmark numbers from staging, confirm outstanding access and security items, align on next steps for a short load run and decision timeline.

Topics: onboarding progress, staging access, SAML/SSO, VPC peering, p50/p95 latency, KV cache warmup, dedicated vs hosted pilot economics, SOC2 docs.

[00:00] Jamie: okay everyone, thanks for joining, uh let's do a quick check-in on the pilot gate, we had a few tickets opened last week and wanted to see where we stand on access and the bench numbers.
[00:18] Priya: hi hi, thanks, quick note, team put in the peering request yesterday, and Diego confirmed firewall rules, but we're still blocked on SAML metadata.
[00:28] Samir: got it, thanks Priya. From Redwood's side we provisioned the staging endpoints and ran the first inference sweep this morning — logs are in the shared folder link (see drive:bench-results-05-21). Some notes: prefix cache warmup took about 12 minutes on our run.
[00:46] Alex: when you say prefix cache warmup, do you mean KV cache on the Redwood runtime or application-side caching? because our prompts have a lot of repeated prefix tokens.
[00:55] Samir: yeah it's the KV cache in the runtime, so initial runs will be slower. Once warmed p50 drops by ~30%. Our numbers: p50 ~48ms, p95 ~230ms, p99 ~420ms for the test profile (short chat messages, 128 context).
[01:15] Maria: okay that's helpful. The p95 is a little high for our SLAs, what's contributing?
[01:22] Samir: two main factors — cold KV and network egress in the staging VPC. We also saw occasional queuing when concurrent requests spiked above the pilot concurrency (we configured continuous batching at moderate levels). We can tune batching window and reduce p95 at cost of slightly higher p50.
[01:40] Jamie: yes, tradeoff note — latency vs unit cost. If you lean into tighter SLOs (lower p95) you may want dedicated capacity with lower queuing variability, but that increases committed spend.
[01:56] Priya: on the security front, you'll need to share SOC2 docs and we need to surface KMS integration details — our security team won't sign off without HSM details.
[02:06] Jamie: absolutely — I'll send the SOC2 snapshot and the security pack. Samir, can you include KMS/HSM integration notes?
[02:12] Samir: yeah, will add a short diagram showing key flow and where audit logs land. Also note that our private deployment option supports customer-managed keys.
[02:24] Diego: small interruption — our networking team noticed some DNS timeouts hitting the staging endpoint intermittently, might be related to egress NAT.
[02:33] Samir: thanks, Diego, we saw a few socket timeouts in the trace; Samir (me) — I'll re-run with tcpdump and forward the packet captures.
[02:42] Alex: can you also include request traces with KV hit/miss markers? that will help us understand cache dynamics.
[02:48] Samir: yes, will add KV hit/miss annotation and include token-level latency breakdown per call.
[02:55] Maria: what about data residency — we need EU-only for some workloads. Does Redwood dedicate region pinning?
[03:03] Jamie: yes, you can pin region and we have private deployments that stay in customer VPCs for EU residency. We'll share region pinning steps.
[03:11] Alex: back to numbers — can you run a 1-hour load test simulating our concurrency and share p50/p95/p99 and the cost estimate? That will help the execs decide between hosted and dedicated.
[03:23] Jamie: agreed, Samir, can you own that?
[03:26] Samir: yes I'll run the 1hr test in staging with your concurrency profile and upload the results to the folder by Mon/Tues.
[03:33] Priya: about SAML — we'll send metadata but our IdP needs the ACS URL and cert thumbprint; can you confirm endpoint?
[03:40] Samir: we'll provide ACS URL and a pem for cert. Jamie will include in the checklist.
[03:46] Diego: one more infra item — can Redwood support a short-lived dev token rotation for our platform engineers? we want to avoid long-lived keys on CI.
[03:55] Jamie: yes, we have short-lived tokens and RBAC controls; Samir will attach a sample rotation script for your CI.
[04:03] Samir: note — we also recommend token-level tracing to tie calls back to user routes; it helps triangulate slow requests.
[04:11] Alex: any blockers on the Redwood runtime side for quantization? we run some half-precision models and want to understand if quantization will change latency/cost.
[04:20] Samir: quantization helps cost but may increase p95 variability in some cases. We can do a small A/B using a quantized variant and compare quality metrics. We'll include quality/accuracy deltas in the bench run.
[04:31] Maria: timeline question — when do you need a go/no-go for Dedicated pilot? management wants a decision within two weeks.
[04:38] Jamie: understood. If we can get the load test results and SOC2 pack in the next four business days, that should align with your two-week decision window.
[04:46] Priya: sounds good. we aim to get SAML metadata to you by Friday.
[04:52] Jamie: great. Recap of next steps and owners, and then we'll close:
[05:00] Jamie: (recap) 1) Jamie to send SOC2 snapshot + security pack and KMS/HSM notes by 2026-05-24; 2) Samir to run 1hr staging load with concurrency profile, KV annotations, and packet captures by 2026-05-25; 3) BrightLedger (Priya/Diego) to share SAML metadata and firewall rules by 2026-05-23; 4) Maria to confirm pilot commitment preference by 2026-06-01.
[05:30] Maria: yep that matches. Also please include the pricing sheet for Dedicated monthly commit vs Hosted burst pricing in the pack.
[05:40] Jamie: will include pricing scenarios and a simple cost model.
[05:46] Alex: one ask — include a brief section in the pack on rollback/fallback behavior if Dedicated nodes degrade, e.g., fallback to a compatible hosted variant. We need graceful degradation documented.
[05:58] Samir: good point. I'll include fallback playbook and A/B rollback steps.
[06:05] Diego: any others? if not we're good.
[06:10] Jamie: thanks everyone, we'll circulate the notes and link to the bench folder. Follow up meeting tentatively 2026-05-28 for tune deep-dive.
[06:16] Priya: thanks all.
[06:20] Alex: thanks.
[06:24] Jamie: bye everyone.

Action items (in transcript): Jamie to send SOC2 and security pack; Samir to run load test and attach traces; BrightLedger to send SAML metadata and firewall rules.
